newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks tumble at open, high techs hit.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks tumble at open, high techs hit.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 20068.81 -243.42 LME CASH NICKEL US$7184 -6.0
CANDLR 1.3785 LME CASH ALUM US$1602 -9.5
CAN 30-YR 111.05 +0.30 BRENT CRUDE US$19.38 -0.10
* Toronto stocks lost more than 50 points at Friday's open, pulled down by a tumbling Wall Street after Intel forecast a lower Q2. * 9.7 million shares traded worth C$180 million.

Toronto stocks quickly tumbled at Friday's open as Wall Street and Canadian high technology issues were taken down by investors after Intel Corp warned that its second quarter results would disappoint.
"The tech stocks have set the tone," one equities trader said. "Intel had the bad numbers and they're smacking them."
While Toronto's market lost more than 50 points, Wall Street shed more than 70 or one percent.
Intel lost about US$17 to US$146 in early trading and Canadian high-tech stocks were pulled down as well.
Toronto is also been jittery ahead of Monday's Canadian federal election, contributing to the sell-off, another trader said. "Our market is still weak with the election coming up," he said.
The reigning Liberal Party is forecast to cling to its government majority while the right-wing parties are fighting for second place.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-groups lost territory except for retail. Conglomerates lost the most, followed by golds, utilities and base metals.
Declining issues beat out winners 256 to 158 while 208 traded flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* High technology firm Northern Telecom Ltd dropped 1.95 to 114.80 in moderate trading while Newbridge Networks Corp dipped 0.80 to 53.70.
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc., Canada's largest publicly traded firm, fell 0.50 to 36.15 on 1.3 million shares, pulling the rest of the market south.
* Heavyweight bank stocks continued to sell off, led by Canada's largest. Royal Bank of Canada shed 0.70 to reach 59.05.
* United Grain Growers Ltd rose 0.60 to 15.00 in active trading after news that U.S. giant Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. took a stake of up to 45 percent.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
